evidence.quote: let ensureNotBlocked activity memberId (library: Library) : Result<unit, LendingError> =
| Ok [ "borrow"; m; c ] -> UseCases.borrow ports m c |> render showBorrow

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Change set 1 puts the blocking rule in Tier 2. Accounts.ensureNotBlocked is built on the existing isBlocked, and Loans.borrow, Holds.place and Loans.renew call it (renew calls it before the DECISION-REF reasons). The blocked activities are a closed alternative in Tier 1 (BlockedActivity, MemberBlocked). It also removes the CLI's own copy of the rule, which summed fines and payments and compared them with 5.00m. Tier 3 (Views.members, Views.standing) only calls Accounts.isBlocked and Accounts.owed. Tier 4 only picks text based on the view's Blocked flag.

evidence.quote: let renew ports (copyId: string) : Result<Views.RenewView, LendingError> = commit ports (fun today library -> Loans.renew today (CopyId copyId) library
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Change set 1 adds no effect below Tier 4. The new renew and standing use cases reach the clock and store only through the existing commit/query port helpers. The change also removes code where the CLI called ports.Store.Load/Save, ports.Clock() and Loans.renew directly, a Tier 4 call into Tier 2. The Tier 2 guards are pure.

evidence.quote: let isBlocked memberId (library: Library) = owed memberId library >= Policy.blockingBalance
blocked until it is below {money Policy.blockingBalance}

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Change set 1 defines the blocking balance only once, in Policy.blockingBalance. The block predicate (Accounts.isBlocked) and the amount owed (Accounts.owed) are each defined once and used everywhere. The refusal message points at the Policy value rather than repeating 5.00. The change deletes the CLI's duplicate copy of the 5.00m literal and of the fines-minus-payments calculation.

evidence.quote: let blockingBalance memberType = match memberType with | Standard -> 5.00m | Student -> 2.00m | Staff -> 10.00m
let isBlocked (m: Member) (library: Library) = owed m.Id library >= Policy.blockingBalance m.Type

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Change set 2 makes the blocking balance depend on member type, and that rule sits entirely in Tier 2 (Policy and Accounts). Tier 3 views only pass the member to Accounts.isBlocked. The refusal's limit is carried in the Tier 1 error value (MemberBlocked ... limit), so it is not worked out again outside Tier 2. Tier 4 is unchanged.

evidence.quote: Error(MemberBlocked(m.Id, owed m.Id library, Policy.blockingBalance m.Type, activity))

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Change set 2 adds no new effects. Everything it changes is pure Tier 1/2 code, plus Tier 3 projections that call it. No ports and no host code change.

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money limit}

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Change set 2 defines the per-type balances only once, in Policy.blockingBalance. Accounts.isBlocked and ensureNotBlocked both use it. The message no longer reads the Policy value itself; it takes the limit from the error, which Tier 2 filled in from the same function. That way the message and the check cannot disagree. The decision document and the code agree (5.00, 2.00, 10.00).
